pairs.locus: Walter Map, De Mauro et Zoilo (Zoilus 89-92, Maurus 94-97)
pairs.question: Quid est quod ex otio praemium speratis, quod laborem debitum requie mutatis?
pairs.answer: In umbrosis vallibus vos cum sitis siti, ad laborem liberum satis est eniti; non ho mittit Beemoth glaream Cociti; procul hinc sunt hospites, procul parasiti.
pairs.derivation: Speaker label 'Z.' (Zoilus) introduces the question stanza; he genuinely asks why monks expect reward from leisure, swapping owed labor for rest. Question span trimmed to the two contiguous interrogative lines; the stanza's following lines ('est fortasse regula rea vanitatis, rasis assit habitus, et est vobis satis') are a declarative jibe, dropped. Maurus's reply ('M.' label stripped) answers that they do labor in their shady valleys. Answer taken to the first full stop, which is the end of the stanza ('parasiti.'); the first sentence ends only on a semicolon ('eniti;'), so the window runs through the whole stanza per the full-stop rule. Maurus's next stanza ('Conclusos in gremio populosae polis...') begins a new elaboration and is cut.

pairs.locus: Walter Map, De Mauro et Zoilo (Zoilus 129-132, Maurus 134-137)
pairs.question: Sed per diverticula quid tergiversaris? De jocosis cantibus obicem furaris? Quae laus in ecclesia cantus saecularis? Sapienter psallite coram sacris aris.
pairs.answer: Non est jocus saeculi cantus gregis mei; hymnus est qui excitet animos plebei, non ut plebi placeat, sed ut Deus ei; ad hoc per se jubilat sanctus agnus Dei.
pairs.derivation: Speaker label 'Z.' stripped. Zoilus's preceding stanza ('Nos ex omni genere nuptias implemus...') is self-description, not a question, so the question span starts at the contiguous interrogative block, including 'Quae laus in ecclesia cantus saecularis?' (what worth has secular song in church?). Maurus's reply ('M.' stripped) directly answers that his flock's song is no worldly jest but a hymn to rouse the people toward God. Answer taken to the first full stop at the end of the stanza ('agnus Dei.'); Maurus's next stanza ('Plebs ad nos qui confluit...') elaborates further and is cut.
